title: Cap. VI Arg. 11: Arminian foresight election — no operative force left for the way
pass_a_gloss: Now on the contrary let us weigh this election which the Arminians invent, from the antecedent foresight of persevering faith. Such election takes away all operative force of election, as regards the elect to be conserved or promoted in the way of salvation. For those who are not elected to life except from the intuition of preceding perseverance performed unto the last breath, to them election conferred nothing toward finishing this course in faith and holiness. For they are understood to have overcome all difficulties, and to have arrived at the very threshold of heaven, before they are predestinated by God to life or the heavenly kingdom. But that all the saved went on in the way of faith and holiness, stretched straight to the kingdom of heaven, and all but penetrated within the gates, before they were predestinated by God to life, or by virtue of their predestination received any special grace from God, is plainly horrendous, and intolerable to Christian ears, which gladly admit that of the Apostle: Whom he predestinated, these he also called; whom he called, these he also justified; whom he justified, these he also glorified, Rom. 8:30.
pass_b_english: Weigh by contrast the Arminian invention — election from prior foresight of persevering faith. That sort of election strips election of all operative force for keeping or advancing the elect on the way of salvation. If they are elected to life only by regard to perseverance already kept to the last breath, election gave them nothing toward finishing the course in faith and holiness. They are taken to have overcome every difficulty and reached heaven's very threshold before God predestines them to life. That all the saved pressed on in faith and holiness, aimed straight at the kingdom, and all but entered the gates before they were predestined — or received any special grace by virtue of predestination — is plainly horrendous, intolerable to Christian ears that gladly hear Paul: whom he predestined, he also called; whom he called, he also justified; whom he justified, he also glorified (Rom. 8:30).
source_text: Jam e contra pensitemus hanc, quam fingunt Arminiani, electionem, ex antecedanea fidei perseverantis praevisione. Talis electio tollit omnem vim operatricem electionis, quoad electos in via salutis conservandos aut promovendos. Nam qui ad vitam non eliguntur, nisi ex intuitu praecedentis perseverantiae ad extremum usque halitum praestitae, illis electio nihil contulit ad hunc cursum in fide et sanctitate consummandum. Omnes siquidem difficultates superasse intelliguntur, atque ad ipsum limen caeli appulisse, priusquam a Deo ad vitam sive regnum caeleste praedestinentur. Omnes autem salvandos perrexisse in via fidei et sanctitatis, recta ad regnum caelorum tetendisse, et tantum non intra portas penetrasse, priusquam a Deo ad vitam praedestinati fuerint, aut virtute praedestinationis suae ullam specialem gratiam a Deo acceperint, horrendum plane est, et Christianis auribus intolerandum, quae libenter admittunt illud Apostoli: Quos praedestinavit, hos et vocavit; quos vocavit, hos et justificavit; quos justificavit, hos et glorificavit, Rom. viii. 30.
